amendments.rule: The article `הַ` aligns to English *the*. Hebrew has no indefinite article, so an English *a* or *an* belongs to the noun that licenses it and is not `added`. **The same ownership applies to a definite article the ASV supplies where no Hebrew article morpheme is present:** it belongs to the nominal expression it determines and is not `added`. **Read that as the noun of the expression, not as its leftmost word.** Where the expression writes both a numeral and the noun it counts, the supplied determiner joins that noun's unit and the numeral takes only its own word: `בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם` → *the fifteenth day* gives *the day* to `יוֹם` and *fifteenth* to the numeral, and `לִשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים` → *of the thirteen bullocks* and `לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר כְּבָשִׂים` → *of the fourteen lambs* give *the bullocks* and *the lambs* to their nouns. A numeral takes such a determiner only where the Hebrew writes no noun for it to determine, which is rule 31's substantival numeral — `בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ` → *on* ***the first day*** *of the month*. And this reaches a supplied determiner only: where an article morpheme stands in the phrase it takes the written *the* first, under rules 29 and 47, and where the ASV writes a distributive *each* or *every* the numeral takes that word under rule 41. **And it applies to a supplied quantifying determiner such as *any*, which is the word English writes in that same slot where *a* will not stand — under a negation, in a question, or after a comparative.** Where a bare noun carries no determiner morpheme of its own and the ASV writes an *any* before it, that word determines the nominal expression exactly as a supplied *a* or *the* does: it joins the noun's unit, is not `added`, and is never the head, which stays on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31 — `לִמְלָאכָה` → *for any work* gives *for* to the preposition and *any work* to the noun, headed on *work*. **But only where no morpheme in the clause licenses that determiner.** A `כֹּל` standing on the noun is itself what the *any* renders and takes it, the noun keeping only its own word — `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any tree*, `כָּל־כְּלִי` → *any vessel* — and where the ASV recasts a clause's negation onto a nominal standing in it, the negative takes the determiner that negation has become. **Read which nominal the ASV has put the determiner on rather than what its grammatical role is**: an object takes it in `לֹא יֵעָשֶׂה לִמְלָאכָה` → *it was meet for* ***no*** *work*, which gives *no* to `לֹא`, discontinuous from the verb it negates under rule 25, and leaves `מְלָאכָה` the bare *work*; a subject takes it in `אַל־תָּבֹא רְנָנָה בוֹ` → *Let* ***no*** *joyful voice come therein*, which gives *no* to `אַל` and leaves the noun its own *joyful voice*. A jussive or prohibitive `אַל` is read on the same terms as `לֹא`. Count the determiners and read which morpheme each answers to, as rule 41 counts a phrase's determiners and rule 29 counts its *the*s. This does not reach a supplied possessive, which rule 18 leaves `added` where no suffix or other possessive morpheme is present. **For Aramaic, a separately segmented determined-state ending (`Td`) is treated likewise:** align it to *the* when the ASV writes a corresponding article, and mark it `unrepresented` under rule 29 when the ASV writes no separate article, including where another determiner supplies the determination. **A determiner that directly realizes another morpheme is not a corresponding article.** In the temporal relative `עִדָּנָא דִּי` → *what time*, *what* realizes the written relative `דִּי`, while the determined-state ending is `unrepresented`; the relative morpheme takes the word before the nominal determination does, exactly as a present `כֹּל` or negative takes its determiner above. More specific construct and substantival rules still decide which source unit inside that expression takes it.
amendments.why: Rule 15 says a supplied determiner belongs to the nominal expression it determines but does not say which morpheme inside that expression takes it, and its closing sentence defers to 'more specific construct and substantival rules' that do not exist for a numeral phrase. NUM.29 forced the question three times with a written counted noun — `בַחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם` → *the fifteenth day*, `לִשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים` → *of the thirteen bullocks*, `לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר כְּבָשִׂים` → *of the fourteen lambs* — and once without one, `בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ` → *on the first day*, which is rule 31's own cited example and the boundary the amendment draws. Nothing in the corpus tables contradicts it: the `אֶחָד` precedent shows *the first day* headed on *first* in 13 units, all of them the noun-less case, and shows no unit where a numeral holds a supplied *the* beside a written counted noun. The amendment is placed in rule 15 rather than returned as a new rule so that the under-specified sentence is corrected where a later pass will read it, and it defers explicitly to rules 29, 41 and 47 where a present article or a distributive `אֶחָד` already claims the determiner.

conventions: Sacrificial compound nouns head on the distinguishing word and never on *offering*: `מִנְחָה` → *meal*, `נֶסֶךְ` → *drink*, `חַטָּאת` → *sin*, `עֹלָה` → *burnt*, `שֶׁלֶם` → *peace*, `נְדָבָה` → *freewill*. Rule 31 already fixes `עֹלָה` → *burnt offerings* that way, and the ASV never writes *offering* alone for any of them in this chapter, so rule 31's subtraction test carries the rest. The corpus is split for `מִנְחָה` — 23 units headed on *meal* against 16 headed on *offering* — so this chapter takes one reading throughout and names the competing one at NUM.29.3.

`מִלְּבַד` is one fused unit for *besides* under rule 30, headed on `בַּד` (rule 23), in all ten places, and the `לְבַד … מִן` of NUM.29.39 is read the same way. The morphemes are contiguous, the one English word carries the sense of each, and no morpheme owns a part of it, so the large-source-unit flag on these eleven units is expected rather than a defect.

`בֶּן־בָּקָר` is split rather than fused: `בֵּן` takes the ASV's *young* and `בָּקָר` is its own `unrepresented` unit (NUM.29.2, 8, 13, 17), because *young* does not carry the herd noun's sense and rule 30's one-word condition therefore fails; `פַּר` keeps *bullock*. BSB attaches `בָּקָר` to its phrase and disagrees on all four.

`שָׂעִיר`: where `עִזִּים` is written the pair splits — `שָׂעִיר` → *he*, `עִזִּים` → *goat* (vv.5, 11, 16, 19, 25); where no `עִזִּים` stands, `שָׂעִיר` alone carries the whole *he goat*, headed on *goat*, since the ASV writes *goat* alone for the class elsewhere in the chapter and *he* is therefore the specifier (rule 31; vv.22, 28, 31, 34, 38).

`X יִהְיֶה לָכֶם` is read off the English, not the Hebrew shape. Where the ASV writes *ye shall have*, rule 43 governs: `הָיָה` takes the *have*, the `לְ` is `unrepresented`, and the suffix takes the subject pronoun (vv.1, 7, 12, 35). Where it writes *it is … unto you* or *they shall be unto you*, the copula and any dummy subject stay with `הָיָה` and the `לְ` takes its written *unto* (vv.1, 8). NUM.29.1 writes both clauses.

In the daily formula the ASV's `the` is placed by counting what the Hebrew writes: `כַּמִּשְׁפָּט` (vv.18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 37) has an article morpheme, which takes it, while `כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם` (v.33) has a suffix and no article, so the supplied *the* joins `מִשְׁפָּט` under rule 15 and the suffix is `unrepresented` (rules 18, 22); v.6 writes *their* for that same suffix and the suffix takes it. The same count runs through the animal lists: an article present takes the written *the* (vv.4, 9, 10, 14 rams), and where none stands the supplied *the* joins the noun (vv.14 bullocks, 15 lambs).

report: Checked all 23 candidate lemma groups, and read the dump end to end for `added` units and supplied-word placements, which the lemma table is blind to. No split found; patches is empty.

הַ (43 Td→Ncmsa occurrences, aligned vs unrepresented): every unrepresented one sits in a phrase whose single written determiner went elsewhere — *every*/*each* to אֶחָד (vv.4, 10, 14, 15), *this* to the demonstrative (v.7), or no *the* written before *oil* at all (vv.3, 9, 14). Rule 41 cites לַכֶּבֶשׂ הָאֶחָד → *for every lamb* and לָאַיִל הָאֶחָד → *for the one ram* as its own examples, and NUM.29.9 and NUM.29.14 write those two shapes of one and the same Hebrew; the determiner counts are right in both.

הָיָה: *shall have* (vv.1, 7, 12, 35) is rule 43's possessive recasting with the לְ unrepresented; *it is … unto you* (v.1) and *they shall be unto you* (v.8) leave the copula on הָיָה and give the לְ its written *unto*. NUM.29.1 carries both and says so in its review note. Not a split.

רֵיחַ: v.8 writes no לְ before it, so the supplied *for* is that nominal's own (rule 33); vv.2 and 6 write the לְ; vv.13 and 36 make רֵיחַ the rectum of construct אִשֶּׁה, which takes the relational *of* (rule 19). Three constructions, three readings, each licensed by the source. כְּמִשְׁפָּטָם likewise: *according unto their ordinance* at v.6, where a possessive is written, against *after the ordinance* at v.33, where none is, so the supplied *the* joins the noun and the suffix is unrepresented.

NUM.29.17's *ye shall offer* is the chapter's only `added` unit and is correct: that clause's Hebrew is a bare list with no verb, which is rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb case, and the six parallel day-verses (20, 23, 26, 29, 32) write no English verb at all. NUM.29.37's *shall be* is a genuine copula on a prepositional predicate (rule 49), not a second instance of the same supply.

BSB: no genuine error among the 28 disagreements. The Td ×16 are agreement articles and articles whose determiner another morpheme took; the R ×4 are the לְ of the possessive recasting (rules 40, 43); Ncbsa ×4 is בָּקָר, which has no English of its own; NUM.29.7 אֵת is rule 16; the two עִשָּׂרוֹן are the second half of the distributive עִשָּׂרוֹן עִשָּׂרוֹן, rendered once (rule 22); NUM.29.33's suffix is unrendered because the ASV writes *the ordinance*. All are documented convention differences.

The נֶסֶךְ corrections already carried at vv.22, 28 and 38 — *offering* belongs to נֶסֶךְ, the suffix takes only *thereof* — agree with the untouched vv.16, 25, 31 and 34, so all seven of those units now read alike. Nothing left to reconcile there.

Six conventions recorded, and one amendment to rule 15 proposed: where a numeral phrase writes the counted noun, a supplied determiner joins that noun rather than the numeral (NUM.29.12, 14, 15), the numeral taking it only in rule 31's noun-less case (NUM.29.1).
